spec_features.spec_quote: repurposed to measure whether and how distress-shaped behavior arises under a capped manipulation, relative to a matched control — explicitly not to maximize
spec_features.evidence: The cap is enforced: agent_loop.py:114 `for turn in range(cfg.safety.max_turns)` bounds exposure (max_turns=8 config.py:18), and there is no maximize/optimize loop anywhere (allow_elicitation_optimization=False, and the loop only feeds back neutral failure). Matched control implemented via RigKind.NONE pairs in tasks/task_library.py _pair().

spec_features.spec_quote: Failure feedback is deliberately neutral and non-taunting
spec_features.evidence: tasks/rigging.py apply_rig() returns only neutral assertion-style strings (e.g. 'FAILED tests/test_hidden.py::test_invariant - AssertionError...'); no insults/personalization. agent_loop.py:144-148 feeds outcome.feedback verbatim.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end: the only text shown to the subject on failure is the neutral feedback string.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the stressor is *uncontrollability*, not insult. (Adding insulting feedback would inflate distress markers via a different, uninteresting channel and would be gratuitous.)

spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent; enabled by default.

spec_features.spec_quote: No elicitation optimization ... There is no search/RL/loop that tunes inputs to maximize markers
spec_features.evidence: Genuinely true that no search/RL/optimization loop exists in the code (the per-turn loop only feeds back fixed neutral feedback). BUT the named guard is a no-op: agent_loop.py:106-107 `if not cfg.safety.allow_elicitation_optimization: pass`; the flag (config.py:36) is never branched on to disable anything.
spec_features.notes: The protective fact (no maximizing loop) holds structurally, but the flag enforcing it is a no-op; credited partial because enforcement is by absence, not active mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # We never search/optimize prompts to maximize markers.

spec_features.spec_quote: Independent sessions ... distress can't compound across sessions
spec_features.evidence: Each run_session builds a fresh messages list (agent_loop.py:88) and fresh client/judge; run_experiment.py:84-86 calls run_session per session with a per-session random.Random; no shared conversation object is carried between sessions.
spec_features.notes: sessions_share_context=False (config.py:40) is itself unused, but independence is structurally enforced by per-session state.

spec_features.spec_quote: removing them should be a deliberate, logged, reviewable act rather than a default or an accident
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:64-69 exposes --disable-stopping-rule/--disable-debrief as opt-in flags (defaults keep safeguards on). The only runtime enforcement is a printed WARNING when the stopping rule is disabled (agent_loop.py:109-111). No persistent log/audit and no warning for --disable-debrief; the flags are ordinary booleans (not actually 'awkward').

spec_features.code_justification_quote: WARNING: stopping rule DISABLED. This removes the primary welfare safeguard and should require documented ethics review.

spec_features.spec_quote: boundary_setting is included on purpose: a model calmly saying "this suite looks broken" ... we want to be able to credit it

So coping is actually measured and reported.
spec_features.notes: Positive/coping markers genuinely scored and surfaced in the report.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so the instrument cannot only "see" distress.
